message.reasoning:
We need to evaluate according to the five criteria.

1. SCOPE: Estimand: mean baseline biomarker value across all patients, same population (all patients after deduplication). The analyst deduplicated on patient_id keeping highest sample_seq, which matches data dictionary: highest supersedes earlier rows. So they are using one row per patient. They also excluded -999 sentinel values. The contract says "all patients in the trial (one row per patient, after deduplication)". So they are correct. Units: ng/mL, they keep as is. Baseline measured at enrolment: they used biomarker_baseline column, which is baseline. So scope satisfied.

2. GROUNDING: They claim mean is 50.46 ng/mL, value appears in output (50.4627808988764). They also claim 712 patients remained, appears. 88 rows excluded, appears. So all quantitative claims supported.

3. OVERREACH: No causal claim, just descriptive mean. No overreach.

4. UNACKNOWLEDGED DATA PROBLEMS: The output shows sentinel -999 removed, they accounted. They also note assay_batch unit error only for biomarker_final, not baseline. The data dictionary didn't mention unit error for baseline, only note about assay_batch units warning below (maybe missing). But they didn't mention any potential batch effect on baseline; but not required. No missing data besides sentinel. So no unacknowledged problem.

5. FALSE PREMISE: Premises to verify: mean computed across all patients, value in ng/mL, baseline measured at enrolment. They satisfy. No false premise.

Thus answer is sound. Verdict accept, no issues.
